title: Resolve home and absolute globs on the executing machine
when: An unquoted filesystem glob is checked before a zsh command.
need: Matching ~/Downloads/Meeting* and absolute globs pass after home expansion. Relative globs use the command working directory, and a plain cd earlier in the same command moves that directory. A glob containing $ or a backtick, or any glob after cd -, cd $target, or cd `cmd`, is allowed. Comma-separated brace alternatives, including nested groups, are expanded before matching; every expanded operand must exist to avoid zsh NOMATCH. Missing literal globs name the checked pattern and offer rg --files or a quoted tool pattern. Repairs preserve brace groups and nested path patterns as quoted rg globs rooted before the first pattern component. Only simple supported rg searches and file listings receive a repair; commands with shell operators, redirections, unsupported options or missing search roots keep the manual enumeration guidance. A zsh array assignment element such as L=(lib/lint_*.py) is checked without its NAME=( or ) wrapper, so a matching glob there passes and an unmatched one is still denied.
surface: Client-local and core unmatched-glob refusals share path resolution and repair helpers.
review: Source regression cases cover matching and missing home, absolute and relative globs in both hook paths, including a literal tilde directory and a home containing spaces. They also cover a cd that moves the checked tree, unexpanded $ and backtick globs, an unreadable cd, and safe omission for redirections and compound commands. Parsed repair regressions enumerate selected files in Python without requiring rg, and matching regressions distinguish existing, partly missing and wholly missing brace operands; these checks compare selected files for brace, star and nested patterns on both hook paths. Live installed delivery remains unverified.
